memory_candidates.content: When a multi-phase propagation plan corrects one finding in a source report (e.g. report 866 finding 5) but that report's own later Decisions/Recommendations sections were written assuming the pre-correction verdict and now read as stale, do not expand the phase's edit into those sections unless they are explicitly named in the plan's Files-to-modify list. Record the staleness via issue-record.sh (kind: issue) instead. This keeps each phase's diff auditable against its own stated scope and avoids silent scope creep across multi-record propagation tasks.

A plan's final verification-only phase ('no file edited in this phase') can legitimately still require an edit when validate-artifact.sh's required-section check (e.g. a missing '## Recommendations' section) fails against an EARLIER dispatch's own deliverable that was never checked before. When this happens, restate only what the phase's own Tasks/verification criteria already name (e.g. follow-up proposals already listed elsewhere in the plan) rather than introducing new substantive content, and record the deviation explicitly against the 'Files to modify: none' line rather than silently treating it as in-scope.
